findings.issue: move_to_stale() moves artefacts BY PATH (`{scan}/{run_id}.jsonl`, `diag/{run_id}.npz`, `ckpt/{run_id}.pt`) while the decision to move comes from a done_index taken once per process start, so it can move the CURRENT generation's freshly written results into _stale/. Confirmed by probe (scratchpad/probe_race.py, PROBE 2): worker A (index contains hash_old) moves the old generation, claims, runs, writes jsonl/npz/ckpt + `done/{run}.{hash_new}.ok`, releases; worker B, holding the same process-start index, later reaches the run, sees is_done(index, run, hash_new)==False and stale_hashes==['hash_old'], and move_to_stale relocates A's fresh results to _stale/hash_old/ (as .1 suffixed copies). Observed end state: `{scan}/{run_id}.jsonl` GONE while `done/{run_id}.{hash_new}.ok` still present, and try_claim succeeded again (release() deleted the lock, so a finished run is freely re-claimable). Consequences on the 16k-run campaign: (a) reconcile and dedup report the run as done while analysis finds no record -> a silently missing run; (b) duplicated GPU-hours re-running finished work; (c) if the duplicate worker is killed by the wall clock the results stay in _stale/ permanently. This is exactly the C-R3 workflow ("change num_epochs and resubmit"), and the module's own integration recipe (campaign/stage0_reports/claims-prov.impl.md line 58: index once per process, is_done, stale_hashes, move_to_stale, then try_claim) prescribes the broken order.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a fresh, per-run recheck primitive and make it mandatory in the recipe: `def is_done_now(scan_dir, run_id, hash8): return any(os.path.lexists(done_path(scan_dir, run_id, hash8, s)) for s in DONE_STATUSES)` (2 stats, paid only for runs about to execute, not per grid point). The runner must then do: cheap index skip -> try_claim -> `if is_done_now(...): claim.release(); continue` -> only then move_to_stale + execute. Document in move_to_stale's docstring that it must be called while holding the claim and only after a fresh is_done_now check, and fix the integrator note in the report. Optionally also make done_index re-read per mop-up pass.

findings.issue: _move() re-raises any OSError whose errno is not EXDEV, and move_to_stale() has no error handling, so two workers moving the same stale run concurrently crash with FileNotFoundError between the `os.path.lexists(src)` check (line 477) and `os.rename` (line 171). This is the normal situation at job start: all NPROC workers of a resumed job build the same done_index, walk the grid in the same order and hit the first stale run simultaneously. Confirmed by probe (scratchpad/probe_race.py, PROBE 1): 4 forked workers over 400 stale runs -> 3 of the 4 died with e.g. `FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] ... '/scan/ckpt/svd_bs128_lr0.01_i0000.pt' -> '/scan/_stale/aaaa1111/ckpt/...'` on the very first run. Unless the integrator happens to wrap the call, that kills most workers of a whole-node allocation seconds after it starts.
findings.suggested_fix: In _move(), treat a vanished source as already-moved: `except FileNotFoundError: return None` (and have move_to_stale skip None results); or wrap the per-file body of move_to_stale in `try: ... except FileNotFoundError: continue`. Add a regression test that races 4 processes calling move_to_stale over the same run_ids and asserts every worker exits 0 and every artefact ends up exactly once under _stale/.

findings.issue: write_manifest() overwrites `manifest/{_safe_name(job_name)}.json` unconditionally (tested as intended at tests/test_claims.py:434-436), but the launcher forks NPROC workers inside ONE SLURM job that share $SLURM_JOB_ID (submit_rebuttal_parallel.sh:36-37, distinguished only by +shard_id). Under the contractually-retained static-shard fallback each worker writes only its own slice (`[s.run_id for s in mine]`, per the report's integration note), so the last writer's manifest replaces the others and read_manifest_union() returns a strict subset of the intended grid. C-R2's whole point is that the union IS the intended grid, so reconcile would then be structurally unable to see never-started runs. _safe_name() also silently maps distinct job names to one file (e.g. 'scan/a' and 'scan_a' both -> 'scan_a').
findings.suggested_fix: Either document and enforce per-worker uniqueness (docstring: job_name must include shard_id/pid; `assert` or warn when overwriting a manifest whose run_ids are not a superset), or make the default name include the shard: `write_manifest(scan_dir, job_name, run_ids)` with job_name built as f"{scan}_{slurm_job_id or 'local'}_shard{shard_id}". Add a test with two workers of the same SLURM job id and disjoint slices asserting the union is complete.

findings.issue: The dedup/stale acceptance test for C-R3 ('change num_epochs and resubmit; every run re-executes and the old files are under _stale/') is only covered at the level of isolated primitives. Nothing tests the composed sequence done_index -> is_done -> stale_hashes -> move_to_stale -> try_claim -> mark_done across two hash generations, and nothing tests it with more than one worker or with an index older than the last completion. That is precisely the gap that lets both high findings through: every individual assertion in test_move_to_stale_moves_every_artefact and test_done_index_status_and_hash_semantics passes while the documented composition destroys results.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one test that simulates two workers sharing a process-start index over a scan that already holds a hash_old generation, following the recipe in the report verbatim, and asserts at the end: exactly one execution per run, `{scan}/{run_id}.jsonl` present and carrying hash_new for every run marked done, and `_stale/hash_old/` containing only hash_old content. Add a second test racing 4 processes through the same sequence.

findings.issue: `start_stamp()['start_time']` is an ISO-8601 string while `claims.claim_info()['start_time']` (claims.py:210) is a unix float, and both are written into campaign bookkeeping (the record vs. the claim/started marker). A reconcile or analysis reader that pulls 'start_time' must know which file produced it.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename one of them (e.g. claims uses 'start_unix' like provenance already does, keeping 'start_time_iso'), so the key name determines the type everywhere.

findings.issue: claim_info()['restarts'] seeds from SLURM_RESTART_COUNT and is then incremented per stale takeover, so the field conflates 'how many times this SLURM job was requeued' with 'how many workers died on this run'. The docstring and the impl report both claim the latter. In a requeued job a first-generation claim already reports restarts=2, and test_stale_takeover_has_exactly_one_winner only asserts restarts==1 with the env var unset, so the conflation is untested. reconcile's 'poison run' heuristic will mis-rank runs.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep two fields: `job_restarts` (from SLURM_RESTART_COUNT, informational) and `takeovers` (= gen, incremented only by try_claim), and have reconcile read `takeovers`.

findings.issue: C-R3 also requires 'Save the resolved Hydra config once per job under {scan}/configs/'. It is not implemented in this track (no configs/ helper in claims.py, no entry in the layout docstring) and it is not listed among the open issues for the integrator, so it can fall through the cracks between this track and the runner track.
findings.suggested_fix: Either add a two-line `write_job_config(scan_dir, job_name, resolved_cfg_text)` next to write_manifest (same atomic-write helper), or state explicitly in the 'Notes for the integrator' section that {scan}/configs/ is unowned.
